title: Sum of Floored Pairs
summary: For an integer array nums, calculate the sum of the floor division of each pair of elements, where the floor function gives the integer part of the division.
statement: For an integer array nums, calculate the sum of the floor division of each pair of elements, where the floor function gives the integer part of the division. The result is given modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Sum floor(nums[i] / nums[j]) over every ordered pair of indices.
reference_solution:
def sum_of_floored_pairs(nums):
    modulus = 1_000_000_007
    maximum = max(nums)
    frequency = [0] * (maximum + 1)
    for value in nums:
        frequency[value] += 1
    prefix = frequency[:]
    for value in range(1, maximum + 1):
        prefix[value] += prefix[value - 1]
    answer = 0
    for denominator in range(1, maximum + 1):
        if frequency[denominator] == 0:
            continue
        quotient = 1
        lower = denominator
        while lower <= maximum:
            upper = min(maximum, lower + denominator - 1)
            numerators = prefix[upper] - prefix[lower - 1]
            answer += frequency[denominator] * quotient * numerators
            quotient += 1
            lower += denominator
    return answer % modulus

hints: Equal values can be grouped because they contribute identically as denominators.
For denominator d, numerators in [q*d, (q+1)*d-1] contribute quotient q.
Use value frequencies and prefix counts to count each quotient interval quickly.
The quotient intervals partition all positive numerators, and multiplying by the denominator frequency accounts for every ordered index pair exactly once.
